annotations.text:
OPTION A — Refined Monochrome

The app's current tokens, tightened. Greyscale surfaces, hierarchy carried entirely by type weight and spacing; album art is the only colour on screen.

Why: artwork gets to be the subject. Ages well, never fights the covers, cheapest to build — it is where the code already is.

Tradeoff: little brand personality. Play state and active nav are quiet, so "what is playing" reads slower than in B or C.

OPTION B — Dark + Single Accent

Near-black canvas, one amber accent reserved strictly for signal: active nav, progress, the play button, and whatever is currently playing. Nothing decorative uses it.

Why: the accent becomes pure signal — you always know what is playing and where you are. Gives MadMusic a recognisable identity.

Tradeoff: one colour must suit every album; the accent occasionally clashes with a cover. Pick it deliberately — the chips above the artboard let you try alternatives.

OPTION C — Artwork-Tinted

The UI samples colour from the current album art: a wash behind the content, translucent glass surfaces, tinted player bar. Change the tint chips to see it follow a different cover.

Why: the most expressive and the most "premium music player". Every album makes the app feel different.

Tradeoff: the most work — needs colour extraction in Rust, contrast guarding so text stays legible on any cover, and blur/backdrop-filter that costs GPU on lower-end machines.

Same layout and content in all three on purpose — the only variable is the visual treatment, so the comparison is fair. All three use the app's real tokens: 0.35rem radii, Inter / Montserrat, 256px sidebar, 88px player bar. Pick one, or mix (e.g. A's restraint with C's tinted player bar).
